sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Preserve all prior repairs, including the conditional load-length branch and distinct horizontal coverage. The vertical coverage remains insufficient: the requirement calls for several vertical locations between the UIWL-centred and 0.5h0-below-LIWL cases, but the current SPARQL requires only one intermediateVerticalPosition case. Add a bounded SHACL constraint requiring at least two distinct directAnalysisCase nodes with verticalLoadPositionType nltl:intermediateVerticalPosition, while retaining the three mandated vertical alternatives and same-case ownership/evidence structures. Do not impose an exact total case count or invent terms.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Reject: the graph does not faithfully encode the required direct-analysis position coverage. Each directAnalysisCase must identify the mandated vertical position alternatives (UIWL-centred, 0.5h0 below LIWL, and intermediate positions) and horizontal alternatives (including mid-span or spacing-centred positions), using the supplied controlled position terms and/or the declared UIWL/LIWL reference operands. Numeric verticalLoadPosition and horizontalLoadPosition alone are an unsupported presence-only approximation and do not establish those relationships. Preserve the existing ship-to-case ownership and conditional loadPatchLength/iceLoadAreaFactorCa pairing, but add the required position-type/value structures without inventing new terms.

Preserve the prior position-coverage repair: the controlled vertical and horizontal position structures now address that instruction. However, correct the load-length applicability alternatives. When loadLengthDeterminedFromArrangement is true, do not require loadPatchLength on every directAnalysisCase; when it is false, require several distinct directAnalysisCase nodes, each containing both loadPatchLength and its corresponding iceLoadAreaFactorCa on the same case node. Keep the shared case-node pairing and the required combined bending/shear and capacity-minimizing evidence. The current unconditional sh:minCount 3 case requirement is also too rigid unless the verified requirement independently fixes exactly three cases; encode the required several-case coverage without inventing an exact count.

Preserve the prior conditional load-length repair: the true branch must not require loadPatchLength or iceLoadAreaFactorCa, while the false branch must keep both properties on each case. The remaining graph does not faithfully encode several horizontal locations: it only requires one mid-span-or-spacing-centered case, and the global sh:minCount 2 does not ensure an additional distinct horizontal location because cases may share the same horizontal type. Add a non-conjunctive bounded coverage constraint requiring several distinct horizontal directAnalysisCase nodes, including the mandated mid-span-or-spacing-centered location, without inventing an exact count. Keep the existing controlled vertical coverage, case ownership, same-case length/ca pairing, and required evidence fields.

Preserve all prior repairs, including the conditional load-length branch and distinct horizontal coverage. The vertical coverage remains insufficient: the requirement calls for several vertical locations between the UIWL-centred and 0.5h0-below-LIWL cases, but the current SPARQL requires only one intermediateVerticalPosition case. Add a bounded SHACL constraint requiring at least two distinct directAnalysisCase nodes with verticalLoadPositionType nltl:intermediateVerticalPosition, while retaining the three mandated vertical alternatives and same-case ownership/evidence structures. Do not impose an exact total case count or invent terms.
